item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This could have easily been a joke with that title, but instead you made it into a serious and thought-provoking story about just how seriously the Foundation takes food preparation. Bravo.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Like others, I came for the joke and got humanity. This was quietly affecting.

It reminded me of how I've been cooking for my husband (tendency towards gout, high blood pressure) and our son (at risk for diabetes). Trying to ensure meals that are both medically appropriate and enjoyable is a stimulating challenge. But a week ago or so, I was out running errands and stopped at a Taco Bell on impulse.

Sweet Christmas, it was like watching fireworks with my tongue. Salt, grease, spices… oh my.

Poor Jacob Mackenzie.

item.title: Nice concept, nice motto

Love that. And I love the concept of food being something important to maintain the Foundation as a good place both for anomalies and for people. +1

item.content:encoded:
I thought this was going to take a humorous approach based on the way this was pitched. It's not bad as it is, it's actually an interesting take on a unique concept that is ignored in practically 95% of articles on the site. This is quaint, and I like that.

Not everything has to be a world ending anomaly. Sometimes it's just about serving delicious foods. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So the idea came out of seeing "pataphysics" and thinking it said "pastaphysics" and then thinking about what a department of pastaphysics would actually be. Then I started writing and it got a lot more serious than I expected.

A little explored part of the Foundation, I think. Hope y'all enjoy it.
